title: The stuck gauge

data.source: The 2400 linear-Gaussian worlds with a sticking sensor of Phoenix study P14-EMPTY1-2026-10-07, rebuilt from the same seeds.

prediction: An estimator that treats a bit-identical repeated reading as no evidence, while still letting the world move on, beats the strongest of three rivals by at least 0.01 on at least 80 per cent of 600 worlds; it must not win where repeats are genuine or where the world really is frozen.
baseline: Three rivals scored the same way: trust every reading (the plain Kalman filter), reject surprising readings (the standard innovation gate), and recognise the repeat but stop everything. The textbook missing-observation filter is what the candidate becomes once a repeat is flagged.
why: The registered threshold was met as computed and the controls behaved as registered, and every stored score was reproduced. But the rule is the textbook missing-observation filter applied after spotting a repeat: Phoenix reads its own pass as a useful reduction, with a ceiling of PASS-0, and so does this room.
phoenix_status: SCORED; receipt awaiting the reviewer. Phoenix claims no verdict word beyond "threshold met as computed". Ceiling PASS-0; rung R4 (declared synthetic); novelty N0; specificity S1. Phoenix: "a useful reduction rather than a CRR-specific effect". The Empty Centre as ontology: not tested (NOT DECIDABLE, register row ND-4).
